label: Rob’s latest title prompt
explanation: Rob’s revised prompt supplied by Iman on September 14, compared on the same 18 development examples.
prompt:
We have built an ontology or work activities. A key element of it  is set of verb-direct object pairs derived by extracting the core verb and direct object from activity descriptions in the O*NET database. These verb-direct object pairs serve as the title of work activities in the ontology. Some are based on a single O*NET description and others on multiple O*NET descriptions. We now seek to improve our ontology with your help. We will provide two inputs:
(1) verb-direct object pair, which serves as the title of a work activity
(2) one or multiple O*NET descriptions that served as the basis for the verb-direct object pair 

Execute the following operations:
(A) If the verb-direct object pair is based on single O*NET description, evaluate whether the current title conveys a clear, intuitively understandable sense of the work activity as depicted in O*NET. If so, confirm that the current title is adequate. If not, propose a new title that is clearer and more understandable, but do not change the initial verb. When creating new titles, select wording that is semantically transparent, as specific as possible, intuitive to a non-expert, and confined to 2-5 words. In all cases, provide a rationale. 
(B) If a verb-direct object pair is based on multiple O*NET description, evaluate whether all of the O*NET descriptions are similar enough that they warrant being grouped in a single category. If so, go on to assess the appropriateness of the title, as described in step (A). If the O*NET descriptions do not warrant being kept together in a single category, group them into more appropriate categories and propose a new title for each, using the same approach described in step (A) for creating new titles. When categorizing O*NET descriptions, create groupings of approximately 5-9, unless there is a strong reason for creating larger or smaller groupings (for example, if a very large number of O*NET descriptions are identical, they should be kept in a single group). If a grouping of O*NET descriptions can still be appropriately linked to the original title, indicate as much. In all cases, give a rationale. 

When considering how well a verb-direct object title captures the essence of a linked O*NET description, focus on the verb and direct object included in the title and ignore others. To take into account O*NET descriptions that contain compound verbs or compound direct objects, we have created verb-direct object pairs that encompass all possible combinations. 

Produce the following outputs:
(A) For verb-direct object pairs based on a single O*NET description, indicate those for which
(i) The current title is adequate and should not be changed. 
(ii) The current title is inadequate and should be changed; in such a case, propose a new title. 
(B) For verb-direct object pairs based on multiple O*NET descriptions, indicate those for which 
(i) The existing grouping of O*NET descriptions and title are both adequate. 
(ii) The existing grouping of O*NET descriptions is adequate but the title is inadequate and should be changed; in such a case, propose a new title. 
(iii) The existing grouping of O*NET descriptions should be restructured; in such a case, propose new groupings and titles for each, and if the current title is still adequate for one of the resulting new groupings, indicate as much.
outputFormat: Output format for the software: return one JSON object with "groups" (a list of objects containing "title", "descriptionNumbers", and "reason") and "reason" (the overall rationale). "descriptionNumbers" contains the numbers of the O*NET descriptions supporting that group. These numbers identify descriptions in this input, not group numbers. Include the current title as a group if the current title is adequate for some or all descriptions. Keep rationales brief.
softwareChecks: Ordinary code checks whether the answer can be read, whether description numbers exist, and whether any description is missing or repeated. It flags empty groups, repeated titles, inconsistent grouping of identical descriptions, titles outside 2–5 words, and changes to the leading verb. A description supporting more than one group is shown as a representation-policy question. The code does not change the model answer, assign missing descriptions, decide semantic correctness, approve a grouping, or write to the ontology. For newly split groups, the code also identifies group sizes outside the approximate 5–9-description target so a person can review the exception rationale. A single homogeneous group is not required to split to meet that target.

groups.title: Conduct Research
groups.reason: The current title remains adequate where no substantive research topic is specified. Duplicate and near-duplicate academic descriptions should remain together.

groups.title: Conduct Environmental Research
groups.reason: Investigates environmental problems, ecosystems, resource conservation, land use, and the environmental effects of production and consumption.

groups.title: Conduct Agricultural Research
groups.reason: Research concerns agricultural production, including crop improvement, plant-based fuels, horticultural methods, and animal nutrition or breeding.

groups.title: Conduct Engineering and Technology Research
groups.reason: Studies the design, performance, or improvement of engineered systems, advanced technologies, materials, and manufacturing or work processes.

groups.title: Conduct Psychological and Behavioral Research
groups.reason: Investigates mental functioning, counseling methods, user experiences, and individual or organizational behavior.

groups.title: Conduct Biological Research
groups.reason: These four descriptions share a focus on cellular biology, genetics, and biotechnology, including interactions between nutrition and genes.

groups.title: Conduct Medical and Healthcare Research
groups.reason: Studies medical conditions and healthcare through clinical, laboratory, nursing informatics, maternal health, and nutritional research.

groups.title: Conduct Therapy and Rehabilitation Research
groups.reason: Groups research in sports medicine, hearing and speech care, and music or occupational therapy around maintaining or restoring function.

groups.title: Conduct Market Research
groups.reason: Examines markets, consumer opinions, buying behavior, product success, and promotional positioning.

groups.title: Conduct Mapping Technology Research
groups.reason: Remote sensing, mapping software, and surveying methods share a geographic-data focus that warrants a small, distinct technology group.

groups.title: Conduct Debt Relief Research
groups.reason: Identifies options for avoiding repossession or foreclosure and lifting debt-enforcement actions—a distinct client-support purpose.

groups.title: Conduct Social and Economic Research
groups.reason: Research concerns economic questions, social issues, social-work knowledge, and theories about societal patterns.

groups.title: Conduct Weather and Climate Research
groups.reason: Both study atmospheric or climate processes, a distinct scientific subject that warrants a two-description group.

groups.title: Conduct Historical and Cultural Research
groups.reason: Studies history and human cultures through historical inquiry, ethnography, anthropology, archaeology, and investigation of historic places.

groups.title: Conduct Donor and Investor Research
groups.reason: These identical descriptions investigate prospective donors or investors, rather than product markets, and should remain together.

groups.title: Conduct Safety Research
groups.reason: Product hazards, industrial hygiene, and fire safety share a safety-focused objective distinct from general technology development.

groups.title: Conduct Background Research
groups.reason: Gathers factual or contextual information to support instructional content, creative work, design, product understanding, or survey topics.

groups.title: Conduct Medical Treatment Research
groups.reason: Explicitly develops, tests, or improves medicines, treatments, surgical techniques, and treatment technologies to prevent or manage disease and injury.

groups.title: Conduct Specimen Preservation Research
groups.reason: Develops specimen restoration and preservation methods, a distinct focus that should not be conflated with historical inquiry or ecological conservation.

groups.title: Conduct Mathematical Research
groups.reason: Extends mathematical knowledge and theory; its distinct subject warrants a standalone group.
